blocks.heading: Where could Block's shares be by October 2029?

paragraphs.text: Block’s weighted value is below today at the first two dates, then roughly recovers by the third. The weighted price is $66.69 at the first date, down 14% with dividends. It rises to $72.78 at the second date, down 7%. At the third, it reaches $79.75, a 2% gain.
The bear case has a 30% probability. The base case has 50%; the bull case has 20%. The October 2029 range runs from $34.28 in the bear case to $141.94 in the bull case.

blocks.heading: What has to go right or wrong for Block?

paragraphs.text: The bear case requires weaker consumer and merchant demand, loan losses or compliance costs that absorb operating savings, and reduced buybacks. Investors then lower the multiple as growth and cash conversion disappoint. The price reaches $47.50 at the first date and $34.28 at the third. Its probability is 30% because recent losses and compliance exposure make sustained equity reduction credible, although historical equity growth argues against making it the central path.

The bull case requires faster Square adoption, deeper Cash App banking use, profitable mature loan cohorts and stronger productivity. Cash generation supports repurchases, while improved execution confidence expands the multiple. The price reaches $91.14 at the first date and $141.94 at the third. Its probability is 20% because the payoff is substantial, but product-level lending returns and durable seller-retention evidence remain limited.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Block really make?

paragraphs.text: Free cash flow usually means operating cash flow less capital spending. That measure improved strongly in 2025 because accounting earnings converted into cash and capital spending remained modest. Cash matters because reported profit cannot repay lenders or fund expansion until it arrives.

earnings.closing: The full memo also explains Block’s business, rivals, management and risks.

paragraphs.text: Management guides to $12,510,000 thousand of 2026 gross profit, up 21%. It guides to $3,470,000 thousand of adjusted operating income, up 67%, at a 28% adjusted operating margin. Adjusted diluted EPS guidance is $4.02, up 70%. Longer term, management targets mid-teens annual gross-profit growth in 2027–2028 and about 30% annual adjusted operating-income growth.

blocks.heading: Did Block keep its past promises?

paragraphs.text: Management made one promise that can be checked. It said in February 2025 that it expected to exit that year at a Rule of 40 run rate. The measure adds gross-profit growth to adjusted operating margin. In the fourth quarter of 2025, growth was 24% and adjusted operating margin was 20%. Together, they cleared the 40-point test.

blocks.heading: What do Block’s last eight quarters show?

paragraphs.text: Revenue grew from the prior year, while gross margin also improved. Gross profit rose broadly, with Cash App growing faster than Square. That combination is healthier than payment volume rising without additional retained profit.

Reported operating income nevertheless fell, and net income fell more sharply. Contingencies, restructuring and other charges totalled $365,118 thousand in June 2026. Removing that category alone would raise operating income, but the category includes regulatory matters and impaired assets that may not be economically disposable.

blocks.heading: What should I watch in Block’s next results?

paragraphs.text: The next scheduled results date is November 3, 2026. The September-quarter report should show whether Block delivered its 28% adjusted operating margin while expanding investment. The important follow-through is customer activity and cash conversion: a launch matters financially only when customers return and the resulting income exceeds acquisition, servicing and credit costs.
